name: @scottish-tides/mobile
//packageManager: Pin npm to the version node 24 ships, which is what devenv and CI both use. Dependabot runs npm through corepack and honours this. Keep it in step with the node version everywhere else (devenv.nix, the workflows): a lockfile written by npm 11 fails `npm ci` under npm 10 with "Missing: <pkg> from lock file", which broke every grouped PR until this pin existed.

scripts.//lint: `expo lint` (the wrapper) resolves eslint-config-expo's nested deps from its own module context and fails; calling eslint directly is what the wrapper does anyway. eslint-import-resolver-typescript and @typescript-eslint/parser are direct devDeps for the same reason — eslint-plugin-import requires both by bare name from the project root, and npm nests them under eslint-config-expo where that lookup misses them (the error is a wall of bogus `Parse errors in imported module`). eslint and typescript are held below their latest majors: see the ignore list in .github/dependabot.yml.
scripts.//test:unit: Every *.test.ts anywhere in the app (node excludes node_modules). The old `lib/*.test.ts` was non-recursive, so a test added under components/, hooks/ or any new lib/ subdir would never have run — in CI least of all. This re-runs the engine parity tests too (~0.3 s); test:engine stays as the focused script for engine work, and as its own named CI step.
scripts.//build:android: Release APK. The script enters devenv itself, prebuilds if android/ is missing, and fixes the NixOS aapt2. Env: PREBUILD=clean to regenerate android/, ABI=arm64-v8a for a much smaller/faster build.

android.//exclude: expo-location pulls in the proprietary play-services-location, which F-Droid forbids. Android uses modules/platform-location instead; iOS still links expo-location.
android.//buildFromSource: Expo modules ship precompiled AARs (node_modules/*/local-maven-repo) and Android links those by default. F-Droid builds everything from source, so compile every module here too — the GitHub APK then matches F-Droid's.

//overrides: uuid is transitive and build-time only (ionicons → @expo/config-plugins → xcode, used by `expo prebuild`), never bundled into the app. Dependabot can't fix it: every path it can take still resolves a vulnerable uuid, so it errors instead of opening a PR. xcode only calls uuid.v4(), which 14.x still exports, so pinning it here is safe. Drop this once xcode ships a modern uuid.
